Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment (2305.11206v1) · paper method: The quality/diversity/quantity ablations fine-tune 7B models and use ChatGPT scores; the paper explicitly acknowledges possible confounding when using Stack Exchange versus wikiHow as a diversity proxy.

cohort3.claim.lima.ablation-scope

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific author-reported study; experiments, raw dataset records and formal proofs were not independently reproduced or verified.
  • The source comparison does not isolate diversity alone, and the result does not establish universal diminishing returns to instruction data.
  • LIMA: Less Is More for AlignmentLocator: Physical PDF pp6-8, section5 and Figures5-6; excerpt at physical p6, pdftotext-layout line 53 (1-based).

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment (2305.11206v1) · paper method: In the paper’s human preference evaluation over 300 test prompts, LIMA versus April-2023 GPT-4 responses records 18% wins, 25% ties and 57% losses.

cohort3.claim.lima.dated-human-comparison

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific author-reported study; experiments, raw dataset records and formal proofs were not independently reproduced or verified.
  • Wins plus ties are 43%; this is not a 43% win rate or a current product comparison.
  • LIMA: Less Is More for AlignmentLocator: Physical PDF pp4-5, section4.1 and Figure1; excerpt at physical p5, pdftotext-layout line 22 (1-based).

LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment (2305.11206v1) · paper method: The discussion identifies substantial manual curation effort and limited robustness: unlucky decoding samples or adversarial prompts can produce weak LIMA responses.

LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment (2305.11206v1) · paper method: LIMA fine-tunes pretrained LLaMa 65B on exactly 1,000 curated demonstration sequences; Table 1 separates community-derived examples, 50 Natural Instructions examples and 200 paper-author training examples.
